name: Making Sure AI Reasons Correctly Step by Step
gist: Papers evaluate whether language models actually think through problems logically, trace their reasoning faithfully, and catch when they make mistakes — rather than just guessing the right answer.
explain: When you ask an AI to solve a math problem or debug code or work through a logic puzzle, you do not just care whether it gets the right answer. You also care whether it actually reasoned through it step by step, the way a human would, or whether it just pattern-matched an answer from its training data. This is especially important for high-stakes problems: if a model recommends a medical treatment, you want to know whether it traced through the logic or just guessed based on surface features. This subtheme is about building tests for genuine step-by-step reasoning.

The core challenge is that it is hard to know what the model is really thinking. A model might write out steps that look right, but they might be a post-hoc story it is inventing after having already settled on an answer. You need benchmarks that actually test whether reasoning is genuine: Can the model catch its own mistakes partway through? If you change a small detail in the problem, does it redo the reasoning, or does the answer stay the same? Does the reasoning trace the logic faithfully, or does it skip steps and hide confusions? These tests require creating problems where the reasoning path is as important as the final answer, and where you can verify the model actually followed that path.

Researchers tackle this by building datasets where the reasoning steps matter. Some gather multi-step math or logic problems where the intermediate reasoning can be checked. Others create benchmarks for domains like theorem proving or scientific reasoning, where you can verify whether the logic is sound. A few build adversarial tests: change one number in a math problem and see if the model catches where its earlier steps no longer apply. The goal is to move past just measuring right answers toward measuring genuine reasoning.

papers.title: AFD-INSTRUCTION: A Comprehensive Antibody Instruction Dataset with Functional Annotations for LLM-Based Understanding and Design
papers.contribution: Instruction-tuning demonstrates consistent improvements across diverse antibody-related tasks, establishing a foundation for antibody modeling and therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: CogniLoad: A Synthetic Natural Language Reasoning Benchmark With Tunable Length, Intrinsic Difficulty, and Distractor Density
papers.contribution: Identifies task length as dominant constraint and reveals varied tolerances to intrinsic complexity and U-shaped responses to distractor ratios across 22 reasoning LLMs.

papers.title: Cost-of-Pass: An Economic Framework for Evaluating Language Models
papers.contribution: Reveals that lightweight models excel at basic tasks, large models at knowledge-intensive tasks, and reasoning models at complex quantitative problems, with cost halving every few months.

papers.title: Don’t Pass@$k$: A Bayesian Framework for Large Language Model Evaluation
papers.contribution: Faster convergence and greater rank stability than Pass@k on benchmark datasets (AIME, HMMT, BrUMO) with clear decision rules for statistical significance.

papers.title: Exposing Weaknesses of Large Reasoning Models through Graph Algorithm Problems
papers.contribution: Reveals accuracy falls below 50% once graphs exceed 120 nodes; demonstrates over-thinking phenomenon driven by extensive yet ineffective self-verification.

papers.title: HSSBench: Benchmarking Humanities and Social Sciences Ability for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art MLLMs struggle significantly with HSS tasks, revealing gaps in cross-disciplinary reasoning and knowledge integration abilities.

papers.title: SPARTA: Scalable and Principled Benchmark of Tree-Structured Multi-hop QA over Text and Tables
papers.contribution: End-to-end pipeline produces thousands of high-fidelity question-answer pairs covering aggregations, grouping, and deep multi-hop reasoning; state-of-the-art models show significant performance gaps.

papers.title: SurvHTE-Bench: A Benchmark for Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation in Survival Analysis
papers.contribution: The benchmark offers the first rigorous comparison of survival HTE methods across diverse conditions and realistic assumption violations.

papers.title: Tab-MIA: A Benchmark Dataset for Membership Inference Attacks on Tabular Data in LLMs
papers.contribution: First evaluation of state-of-the-art MIA methods on LLMs fine-tuned with tabular data shows models memorize structured data making them vulnerable with AUROC approaching 90%.

papers.title: VoxPrivacy: A Benchmark for Evaluating Interactional Privacy of Speech Language Models
papers.contribution: Reveals widespread vulnerability where most open-source models perform near random chance (50% accuracy) on conditional privacy decisions, while even strong closed-source systems fail on proactive inference.

papers.title: WorldEdit: Towards Open-World Image Editing with a Knowledge-Informed Benchmark
papers.contribution: Dataset and methods significantly narrow the gap with GPT-4o and Nano-Banana, demonstrating competitive performance in both instruction following and knowledge plausibility where open-source systems typically struggle.

papers.title: Accuracy and Normalized Accuracy under Length Bias: Analysis, Guidelines, and a Bayesian Alternative
papers.contribution: Provides drop-in replacement for likelihood-based evaluation with consistently lower empirical length bias across benchmarks.

papers.title: Active Policy Optimization for Individualized Dosing via Gradient Variance Minimization
papers.contribution: GVALID achieves superior performance under strict budget constraints on optimal policy learning for individualized dosing.

papers.title: Anytime-Valid Inference for Online Ranking of Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Provides anytime-valid guarantees enabling early stopping with substantial cost savings; extends to top-k model identification.

papers.title: A²RBench: An Automatic Paradigm for Formally Verifiable Abstract Reasoning Benchmark Generation
papers.contribution: Finds that current LLMs severely underperform humans (39.8% vs. 68.5%) on abstract reasoning and struggle with high-dimensional 3D tasks, while higher-information-complexity inputs paradoxically simplify reasoning.

papers.title: Benchmarking LLM Tool-Use in the Wild
papers.contribution: No model achieves accuracy above 15%, revealing substantial gap in LLMs' robustness despite prior benchmarks suggesting progress, emphasizing user-LLM-tool interaction challenges.

papers.title: Beyond the Final Answer: Evaluating the Reasoning Trajectories of Tool-Augmented Agents
papers.contribution: TRACE accurately evaluates complex trajectories using small open-source LLMs and reveals previously unreported observations about agent performance on tool-augmented tasks.

papers.title: CauSciBench: Can LLMs Automate Causal Inference in Real-World Scientific Research?
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that models consistently perform worse on real datasets, revealing the critical bottleneck of causal method selection through evaluation of 7 frontier models on 300+ queries.

papers.title: CodeSense: a Real-World Benchmark and Dataset for Code Semantic Reasoning
papers.contribution: First benchmark for fine-grained code semantic reasoning from real-world projects reveals fundamental gaps in LLM code comprehension despite prompting techniques.

papers.title: Compact Conformal Subgraphs
papers.contribution: Efficient approximation algorithms with constant-factor coverage-size trade-offs while preserving statistical validity via conformal calibration.

papers.title: Demystifying Deep Search: A Holistic Evaluation with Hint-free Multi-Hop Questions and Factorised Metrics
papers.contribution: The benchmark reveals that systems excel at executing given paths but fail to discover them, with EvidenceLoop agentic workflow demonstrating architectural improvements.

papers.title: DocHop: Benchmarking Out-of-domain Multi-hop Reasoning in Information-Dense Documents
papers.contribution: DocHop reveals a substantial gap between human performance (>90% accuracy) and best models (60.18%), with reasoning-enhanced models improving but struggling as complexity increases.

papers.title: Draw-In-Mind: Rebalancing Designer-Painter Roles in Unified Multimodal Models Benefits Image Editing
papers.contribution: DIM-4.6B-Edit achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on ImgEdit and GEdit-Bench benchmarks, outperforming much larger models like UniWorld-V1 and Step1X-Edit.

papers.title: Efficient Bayesian Inference from Noisy Pairwise Comparisons
papers.contribution: Delivers efficient inference with well-calibrated uncertainty estimates and robust rankings even with noisy crowdsourced raters, enabling cost-effective human evaluation.

papers.title: Efficient Inference for Noisy LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation
papers.contribution: Systematically characterizes when PPI-style estimators attain strictly smaller asymptotic variance than measurement-error corrections for mean parameter estimation.

papers.title: Evaluating LLMs When They Do Not Know the Answer: Statistical Evaluation of Mathematical Reasoning via Comparative Signals
papers.contribution: Substantially improves ranking accuracy and precision of performance estimation with gains increasing as model noise grows, demonstrated on GPQA Diamond, AIME 2025, and GSM8K.

papers.title: ExCyTIn-Bench: Evaluating LLM agents on Cyber Threat Investigation
papers.contribution: The best model achieves a reward of 0.606, demonstrating the task difficulty and leaving substantial headroom for future research.

papers.title: FaithCoT-Bench: Benchmarking Instance-Level Faithfulness of Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.contribution: Systematic evaluation identifies strengths/weaknesses of detection approaches and reveals increased challenges with knowledge-intensive domains and advanced models.

papers.title: FiRE: Fine-grained Ranking Evaluation for Machine Translation
papers.contribution: Outperforms regression-based and error-analysis metrics in aligning with human judgments while providing more informative insights on reference-free benchmark.

papers.title: From Knowledge to Inference: Formalizing Specialized Public Health Reasoning on GlobalHealthAtlas
papers.contribution: Provided large-scale multilingual public health dataset with rigorous quality control and reproducible evaluation enabling safety-critical health reasoning research.

papers.title: General Synthetic-Powered Inference
papers.contribution: Error rate remains below a user-specified bound without distributional assumptions on synthetic data, with benefits demonstrated on AlphaFold protein structure prediction and reasoning model comparison.

papers.title: HypoSpace: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Set-Valued Hypothesis Generation under Underdetermination and Sublinear Coverage Bounds
papers.contribution: Reveals capability-dependent coverage failure: models maintain validity while exhibiting reduced uniqueness and recovery as hypothesis spaces become larger.

papers.title: Ice Cream Doesn’t Cause Drowning: Benchmarking LLMs Against Statistical Pitfalls in Causal Inference
papers.contribution: Reveals significant limitations in LLMs for statistical causal inference and provides quantitative metrics to advance development.

papers.title: LEXam: Benchmarking Legal Reasoning on 340 Law Exams
papers.contribution: LEXam reveals LLMs struggle with structured multi-step legal reasoning, provides scalable LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation closely aligned with human expert assessment.

papers.title: LINGOLY-TOO: Disentangling Reasoning from Knowledge with Templatised Orthographic Obfuscation
papers.contribution: Model performance markedly drops upon obfuscation (best reasoning models drop from 0.60 to 0.48), effectively disentangling reasoning from knowledge.

papers.title: LakeQA: An Exploratory QA Benchmark over a Million-Scale Data Lake
papers.contribution: Comprehensive benchmark showing GPT-5.2 achieves only 14.73% exact match, providing realistic testbed for LLM agents that both find and analyze data.

papers.title: Let the Prototype Guide You: Robust Aggregation of Sparse Multi-Class Annotations via Annotator Prototype Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves 26% accuracy improvement in best cases, boosting average accuracy from 68.73% to 74.11% across 10 real-world datasets spanning five domains.

papers.title: LiveNewsBench: Evaluating Web Search Agents with Freshly Curated News
papers.contribution: Provides regularly updated benchmark for rigorous evaluation of agentic web search with public leaderboard, datasets, and code.

papers.title: LongCoT: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.contribution: Reveals substantial capability gap with frontier models achieving <10% accuracy (GPT 5.2: 9.8%; Gemini 3 Pro: 6.1%), establishing rigorous long-horizon reasoning measurement.

papers.title: MECAT: A Multi-Experts Constructed Benchmark for Fine-Grained Audio Understanding Tasks
papers.contribution: DATE metric penalizes generic terms and rewards detailed descriptions via semantic similarity and cross-sample discriminability, comprehensive evaluation reveals audio models' current capabilities and limitations.

papers.title: Multiple-Prediction-Powered Inference
papers.contribution: Consistently achieves lower estimation error than baselines on LLM evaluation tasks through budget-adaptive allocation learning complex cost and correlation structures.

papers.title: Multiverse Mechanica: A Testbed for Learning Game Mechanics via Counterfactual Worlds
papers.contribution: Provides reproducible, low-cost testbed for studying and comparing methods to learn game mechanics beyond pixel reproduction.

papers.title: ODI-Bench: Can MLLMs Understand Immersive Omnidirectional Environments?
papers.contribution: Shows current MLLMs struggle with omnidirectional context, while Omni-CoT training-free method significantly enhances comprehension through chain-of-thought.

papers.title: OmniVideoBench: Towards Audio-Visual Understanding Evaluation for Omni MLLMs
papers.contribution: Evaluation of multiple MLLMs on OmniVideoBench reveals a pronounced gap between model performance and human reasoning, with open-source models significantly lagging closed-source counterparts.

papers.title: ROVER: Benchmarking Reciprocal Cross-Modal Reasoning for Omnimodal Generation
papers.contribution: ROVER reveals that cross-modal reasoning capabilities correlate with visual generation performance, but current models remain limited in visual-augmented reasoning.

papers.title: Reasoning Language Model Inference Serving Unveiled: An Empirical Study
papers.contribution: The study reveals distinct RLLM serving behaviors including significant memory fluctuations and domain preference, showing quantization and speculative decoding improve efficiency while prefix/KV-cache methods may degrade accuracy.

papers.title: RewardEval: Advancing Reward Model Evaluation
papers.contribution: RewardEval provides rigorous evaluation practices and demonstrates how reward model performance on the benchmark correlates with effectiveness in best-of-N sampling and RLHF training.

papers.title: SciTS: Scientific Time Series Understanding and Generation with LLMs
papers.contribution: Shows general-purpose LLMs have stronger generalizability than specialized models; TimeOmni explores how to extend LLMs for scientific time series while maintaining general-purpose training.

papers.title: SimpleToM: Exposing the Gap between Explicit ToM Inference and Implicit ToM Application in LLMs
papers.contribution: Reveals striking gap: state-of-the-art models reliably infer mental states but fail at applying this knowledge, with performance dropping sharply on secondary predictions.

papers.title: Simultaneous Confidence Bounds for Aggregated Effects via Exact Subset Optimization
papers.contribution: Establishes finite-sample coverage guarantee with lighter subset-family dependence than classical methods and demonstrates scalability on synthetic and ML applications.

papers.title: SportR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Large Language Model Reasoning in Sports
papers.contribution: SportR is the first multi-sport large-scale benchmark designed to train and evaluate MLLMs on sports intelligence reasoning with structured QA hierarchies and human-authored reasoning annotations.

papers.title: TRACE: Toulmin-based Reasoning Assessment through Constructive Elements for LLM CoT Evaluation
papers.contribution: Shows strong correlation with benchmark accuracy (r=0.74) and outperforms accuracy-only baselines as a reinforcement learning reward signal across 7 reasoning models on 26.3K samples.

papers.title: The Quest for Efficient Reasoning: A Data-Centric Benchmark to CoT Distillation
papers.contribution: Provides actionable insights on data manipulation effects for in-distribution and out-of-distribution generalization, establishing best practices for optimizing CoT distillation.

papers.title: VideoReasonBench: Can MLLMs Perform Vision-Centric Complex Video Reasoning?
papers.contribution: Comprehensive MLLM evaluation shows most perform poorly on complex reasoning (GPT-4o 6.9% accuracy) while Gemini-2.5-Pro with thinking achieves 56.0%.

papers.title: Zebra-CoT: A Dataset for Interleaved Vision-Language Reasoning
papers.contribution: Fine-tuning on Zebra-CoT yields +12% improvement in test-set accuracy and up to +13% gains on standard VLM benchmarks for native visual reasoning.
